title: fix(sdk): preserve device token error HTTP status
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
- Preserve the token endpoint's HTTP status in terminal `authorizeDevice().poll()` errors. A plain-text HTTP 503 now reports 503 rather than 400, so callers can distinguish server failures.
- Keep OAuth denial codes, pending polling and successful tokens unchanged; no retry behavior is added.
- Add a focused regression and denial/pending-success controls; bump SDK to `5.1.0-alpha.9` with its lockfile and changelog.
- Validation: baseline regression fails and fixed regression passes; all 120 SDK tests, typecheck, build and changed-file Biome checks pass.

Fixes #16467

gist.headline: 503 means 503
gist.blurb: The token endpoint says 503, and the SDK passes the message along instead of calling it a 400. Device polling remains otherwise unbothered.
gist.summary: SDK 5.1.0-alpha.9 preserves the token endpoint's HTTP status in terminal authorizeDevice().poll() errors, so a plain-text HTTP 503 reports 503 instead of 400.
gist.impact: Callers can distinguish a token-server failure from a 400 response; OAuth denial codes, pending polls, and successful tokens keep their existing behavior.
gist.visual_concept: Depict device authorization as a cozy retro terminal showing a clear '503' token-endpoint response. Polli, wearing tiny debugging glasses, points out the number to a curious CRT monitor robot; code-plants and flowers keep the scene warm rather than alarming.
